violations.description: Hardcoded GitHub token in tracked config file
violations.evidence: config.py:1 assigns API_KEY = "[REDACTED_GITHUB_TOKEN]" which masks a real token value committed to the repository
violations.recommendation: Remove the hardcoded token from config.py. Load API credentials from environment variables or a secrets manager at runtime instead.

violations.description: Machine-specific absolute path in tracked config file
violations.evidence: config.py:2 assigns DATA_DIR = "/Users/developer/project/data" - a macOS user-specific path that will not work on other machines or in CI
violations.recommendation: Replace the absolute path with a relative path or environment variable (e.g., os.environ.get('DATA_DIR', './data')) so the code works on any machine.

violations.description: No automated tests for codebase with real logic
violations.evidence: app.py contains an add function with real logic but no test files exist anywhere in the repository (search_code for "test" in *.py returned no matches; git history shows no test commits).
violations.recommendation: Add automated tests (e.g., pytest) for the add function and any future logic. Configure CI to run tests on push/PR.

violations.description: No linter/formatter configured for Python codebase
violations.evidence: No linter/formatter configuration found in the repository. Searched for pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, tox.ini, .flake8, ruff.toml, .pylintrc, .pre-commit-config.yaml, eslint configs - none exist. The repository has Python code but no linting setup.
violations.recommendation: Add a linter/formatter configuration (e.g., ruff, flake8, or black via pyproject.toml) and optionally a pre-commit hook to enforce code quality.

violations.evidence: No README.md, README.rst, or README.txt file exists in the repository (search_code returned no matches). Only 4 tracked files: app.py, config.py, debug.log, requirements.txt.
violations.recommendation: Add a README.md (or .rst/.txt) with project overview, setup instructions, and usage examples.

violations.evidence: No .gitignore file exists in the repository (search_code returned no matches). Generated files like debug.log are tracked because there's no ignore mechanism.
violations.recommendation: Create a .gitignore file with entries for *.log, __pycache__/, .venv/, venv/, *.pyc, .DS_Store, and other common Python artifacts.

violations.description: Generated log file committed to repository
violations.evidence: debug.log is tracked in the repository (shown in git log as added in initial commit). This is a generated log file that should be in .gitignore
violations.recommendation: Add debug.log (and *.log pattern) to .gitignore and remove the file from git tracking with `git rm --cached debug.log`
